hints.title: Name what the axes measure
hints.body: Write X=logx and Y=logy. A straight line on these axes has equation Y=mX+c.
hints.recap: A straight-line relationship applies to the quantities on the axes.
hints.pitfall: The horizontal variable here is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>log</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow></math>, not <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow></math>.
hints.pause: Replace <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>X</mi></mrow></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>Y</mi></mrow></math> with the original logarithms.

recall.reminder: A straight-line relationship applies to the quantities on the axes.

hints.title: Apply the logarithmic power rule
hints.body: The line equation becomes logy=mlogx+c=log(xm)+c. Both original variables must be positive for their logarithms.
hints.recap: A constant multiple of a logarithm moves into its exponent.
hints.pause: Rewrite the equation as a difference of logarithms equal to a constant.

recall.reminder: A constant multiple of a logarithm moves into its exponent.

hints.title: Undo the logarithm
hints.body: Rearrange your line equation so that a difference of logarithms equals the constant intercept. Combine that difference using the quotient law, then undo the logarithm.
hints.recap: Reversing the logarithmic equation reveals the relationship between the original positive variables.
hints.pitfall: An exponential in <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow></math> is linear on a log–ordinary plot, a different choice of axes.
hints.pause: Isolate y and compare the resulting relationship with the listed options.

recall.reminder: Use the quotient law to combine a difference of logarithms, then exponentiate in the same valid base.

solution:
A line on the plotted axes means logky=mlogkx+c, for a fixed valid logarithm base k.

Exponentiating gives y=kmlogkx+c=kcxm. Hence the relation has the form y=axm, where a=kc>0 is constant.

This is the power-law form in D. The positive variables are necessary for the plotted logarithms to exist.
knowledgePattern: Recognise power law on log-log axes
